title: `ia preview` shows what one new record, field or relationship would compile to
summary: @inventarch/cli adds `ia preview` (catalog row: mode validate, move Verification), which writes nothing. `ia preview <word> <name> [<field>=<value>...] [--at <path>]` drafts a new record into --at or <first authored root>/<word>.ia, the first root the repository's `@workspace` declares at authored placement inside .ia/src (`ia preview system <name>` is init's starter system at .ia/src/systems/<name>/system.ia); `ia preview --relate <owned> <spelling> <target>` adds one relationship row and `ia preview --set <owned> <section.key>=<value>` sets one field (`+=` adds one item to a list field) of an owned record: one at authored placement (band 100) in a file under such a root, outside the floor, named by canonical identity or `@word name`. --at must lie under such a root and is judged as the volume spells it: an existing part of the path spelled otherwise (a case variant, an 8.3 short name) is refused, naming the volume's spelling, before the mandate profile or the ownership check reads it. A field is <section>.<key> or a key one schema field alone has; one given twice in either spelling is refused, and a value the shell split is joined again with single spaces. The edit is language's, spliced into the file as it is (other lines keep their bytes and line endings, a byte-order mark stays), and compiled through db's draft overlay against one editor snapshot of the workspace; the output gives the record before and after, the base and candidate revisions, every record of the file with its digest before and after, the file's current sha256 (an absent file reads as empty) and the findings that count against the candidate: the edited or new record's own and any the base does not hold, so an error already in another record or file does not. A record other than the target whose digest would change refuses the preview. `ia preview <word>` prints the word's lowering, schema, default file and consent. Exit 0 for a clean candidate or word guidance, 1 for a candidate with errors. Refusals: a malformed form or an unknown relationship verb is IA-CLI-USAGE at exit 2; IA-CLI-EDIT-INVALID (an unknown word or field, a value of another type or carrying syntax, a field given twice, a duplicate, a nested record, a system already in force), IA-CLI-EDIT-MISSING (no admitted record answers a name), IA-CLI-EDIT-UNOWNED (an installed, adopted or floor record, or a path outside the authored roots), IA-CLI-EDIT-MANDATE (a `@mandate` that binds the acting participant, before or after the edit (its participant is the actor, or it names none and its scope names the workspace or it claims paths), or whose authority the runtime cannot read, naming the governance position) and IA-LANG-EDGE-UNCONSENTED (a row the two-sided consent rule refuses, naming the system whose ledger refuses it) exit 1; IA-DB-PATH-UNSAFE (another spelling of a path, an unsafe path, one holding DEL, a C1 control, a line or paragraph separator or a bidirectional control included, or a link on the way), IA-DB-SOURCE-UNAVAILABLE, IA-DB-SOURCE-CHANGED, IA-DB-DRAFT-INVALID and a workspace that does not open exit 3. A refusal's next command that would repeat a value holding shell syntax ($(...), a backtick, %, a quote, ;) names the word's preview instead; only the invocation's own --root value, as the option before any --, is exempt, and a bare argument opening a comment (#) or a PowerShell splat (@), or holding a comma (a PowerShell array) or a tilde past its start, is repeated double-quoted, while one opening with a tilde, which pwsh expands even double-quoted through an npm-style .ps1 shim, is never repeated. Limits: every printed command repeats the --root value as given, double-quoted only when it holds a space or a quote, so a root path holding a comma or a tilde is printed bare. `ia next` on a workspace that registers `@plan` and authors none names `ia preview plan` where the acting participant's profile allows it, instead of the records to author. The position packet's command catalog gains preview and author rows alongside the integrated command set; the repository's own CLAUDE.md is regenerated from that catalog. A host projection written by 2.0.0 therefore differs from the packet the CLI now renders: after the upgrade `ia doctor` reports it outdated until `ia project <host> --apply`, or `ia host <host> --apply` for a registered host, rewrites it (review C2-N6). Limits: nested records and conditional, structured or internally commented fields are not edited; the --root value is repeated in next commands as every command repeats it; the mandate profile it consults is described in its own note.
